record.body:
## Problem

The loop records a goal, a phase approach, tasks, and a pass/fail check. A passing test is treated as done, and a failure is treated as a coding problem. Specification, design, semantic integration, per-requirement evidence, and the choice of which stage to revisit have no records.

## Approach

Decision: lifecycle-records.

Keep `engage`, `init`, `discuss`, `plan-phase`, `execute-phase`, and `verify-work`. Do not add a skill per stage.

- `discuss` writes one `specification` (what must be true) and one `design` (how it should work), then the decisions a later reader would re-open. Requirements use stable ids `R1`, `R2`, …. `weight` is `light` or `full`. Incidental work skips both records.
- `plan-phase` stamps each work-item with `requirements` and `decisions`, and each acceptance with `requirement`, when a specification exists. Dependencies and waves stay derived.
- `execute-phase` hands the executor the named requirements, design invariants, and decisions. After parallel implementation, and before the verification task, it writes an `integration-report`. A clean git merge does not make that report `pass`. Skip the report when the phase has no parallel implementation wave.
- `verify-work` writes a `check-run` per criterion with `result` `pass`, `fail`, `blocked`, or `insufficient`, plus `requirement` and `evidence_kind` when the acceptance names a requirement. It then writes one `assessment` per requirement: `status` `verified`, `failed`, `insufficient`, or `blocked`; `level` `implementation`, `design`, `plan`, `specification`, `integration`, `verification`, `environment`, or `unknown`; `next` `specify`, `design`, `plan`, `execute`, `integrate`, `verify`, or `release`. A failed check does not automatically return to execute. Three failed assessments for one requirement, or level `environment` or `unknown`, escalate to a blocking question and a finding with `needs` `human`.
- When every assessment for the phase is `verified`, `verify-work` writes `release` state `ready`. Landing may record `merged`. Nothing deploys.
- `feedback` is a signal `engage` can route into specify. Nothing collects it.
- A phase with no specification keeps today's pass/fail check-run path.

Traceability is payload fields plus the existing `informed_by` link: requirement id, decision subject, work-item, check-run, assessment.

This phase edits the bundled contract, the six skills, `skills/ensure-store.md`, the README, and tests. It does not edit the dashboard or the adaptive-artifacts runtime.

Size: more than one.
Stops: plan review before dispatch. No push. No manual sign-off.
Collisions: `contract-loop` owns `contract/project-design.json`, `.artifacts/project-design.json`, and `skills/ensure-store.md`. `specify-design` owns `skills/discuss/SKILL.md`, `skills/init/SKILL.md`, and `tests/test_discuss_skill.py`. `trace-plan` owns `skills/plan-phase/SKILL.md` and `tests/test_plan_trace.py`. `integrate-execute` owns `skills/execute-phase/SKILL.md` and `tests/test_integrate_rules.py`. `assess-route` owns `skills/verify-work/SKILL.md`, `skills/engage/SKILL.md`, and `tests/test_assess_routing.py`. `readme-lifecycle` owns `README.md` and `tests/test_readme_lifecycle.py`. `loop-scenarios` owns `tests/test_evidence_loop.py`. No task edits `dashboard/`, `skills/kinds-and-focus.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or `scripts/close_batch.py`.

## Landing

- branch: `phase/evidence-loop`
- worktree: `/home/andrewyin/se-workflow--evidence-loop`
- base: `main`
- close: commit code on the phase branch, merge into `main`, then commit the store on the primary checkout
- push: not a stop

## Exit criteria

- The bundled contract resolves `specification`, `design`, `integration-report`, `assessment`, `release`, and `feedback`, and `check-run` accepts `pass`, `fail`, `blocked`, and `insufficient` plus optional `requirement` and `evidence_kind`. `uv run --with textual --with pytest python -m pytest tests/test_contract_self_consistency.py -q` passes.
- The six skills document only contract-legal writes. `discuss` writes specification and design. `plan-phase` stamps requirement and decision ids. `execute-phase` writes an integration-report that does not treat a git merge as a pass. `verify-work` writes an assessment whose `next` is `specify`, `design`, `plan`, `execute`, `integrate`, `verify`, or `release`. `uv run --with textual --with pytest python -m pytest tests/test_skill_contract_consistency.py tests/test_discuss_skill.py tests/test_plan_trace.py tests/test_integrate_rules.py tests/test_assess_routing.py -q` passes.
- `tests/test_evidence_loop.py` drives the `adaptive-artifacts` CLI on a fresh store through a verified requirement that ends in release state `ready`; a failed check whose assessment `next` is `execute`; a design-level failure whose `next` is `design`; a third failed assessment that opens a blocking question; an integration-report `fail`; an insufficient assessment whose `next` is `verify`; and a pre-existing `pass` check-run that still validates. `uv run --with textual --with pytest python -m pytest tests/test_evidence_loop.py -q` passes.
- The README describes specify, design, plan, execute, integrate, verify, assess, and release as the skills actually perform them, and describes feedback as a record with no collector. `uv run --with textual --with pytest python -m pytest tests/test_readme_lifecycle.py -q` passes.
